feedback.answered: The public Node experiment observed both schedules from commit=2/applied=1 with node 2 in voters. Before accounting, Campaign stayed follower. With configuration first, Advance yielded applied=2/self_voter=false and Campaign stayed term-1 follower. With Advance first, applied became 2 while self_voter stayed true, and Campaign became term-2 candidate; later configuration callback removed the voter but left the role candidate. Thus Node serialization does not prevent the conditional admission difference. Membership becomes effective upon application according to README and protobuf interface, so commitment alone does not ground an already-removed-node violation.
